d: Responsible for the stable, secure and controlled operation of the Bank’s assigned .NET applications and related services. The role provides end-to-end application support ownership, coordinates incidents, problems, changes and releases, manages technical dependencies and vendors, and ensures service performance, resilience, regulatory compliance and documentation requirements are maintained.
q: Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Information Technology, Software Engineering or a related field.
Microsoft certification relevant to .NET, Azure, application development or cloud operations is an advantage.
Relevant database, DevOps, information security or application-support certification is an advantage.
At least 8 years of application support or technology operations experience, including experience supporting critical enterprise or banking applications.
Practical experience with .NET applications, web services and APIs, SQL databases, Windows-based application environments, monitoring and incident troubleshooting is preferred.
r: Maintain agreed availability, performance and service levels for assigned .NET applications and supporting services.
Ensure critical incidents, recurring problems and production risks are managed within agreed timelines.
Maintain current application ownership records, support documentation, monitoring controls and recovery procedures.
Reduce recurring incidents and operational risk through root-cause analysis, preventive remediation and controlled technical improvements.
Strengthen internal support capability and knowledge retention for critical .NET applications.
Act as the primary support owner for assigned .NET applications, services and technical components.
Coordinate incident, problem, change and release activities across application, infrastructure, database, integration, security and vendor teams.
Monitor application health, performance, capacity, scheduled jobs, interfaces, APIs, logs and operational controls.
Lead investigation of production issues, coordinate root-cause analysis and ensure corrective and preventive actions are completed.
Ensure application patches, framework upgrades, vulnerability remediation, certificate renewals and end-of-life actions are planned and completed.
Coordinate testing, deployment, rollback planning, production readiness and post-implementation validation for application changes.
Maintain application inventories, architecture and interface references, runbooks, support procedures, access matrices and recovery documentation.
Ensure compliance with enterprise architecture, information security, data privacy, change-management, audit and regulatory requirements.
Manage vendor performance, technical support cases, maintenance obligations, service-level commitments and escalations.
Coordinate business continuity and disaster-recovery testing and address identified recovery gaps.
Provide management reporting on service availability, incidents, problems, risks, technical debt and improvement plans.
Ensure effective knowledge transfer and operational handover for new or enhanced .NET applications.
Oversee the release of other non-related technology / application to ensure oversight and additional control as part of segregation of duties.

q: Minimum 10 years of relevant experience in environmental engineering within the power generation industry, either with a power generation company or as part of a consultant/contractor team, preferably on major greenfield projects.
Candidates must possess experience in desalination and power plant projects, as well as marine environmental impact assessments.
Experience managing and coordinating environmental interfaces with third parties and external authorities.
Experience developing and endorsing environmental/HSE specifications and participating in HSE/Environmental studies such as HAZID, EIA, ENVID, HIRA, and dispersion/modelling studies.
Strong knowledge of international environmental regulations, industry best practices, and company specifications/standards.

Experience developing and reviewing Operational or Construction Environmental Management Plans (CEMP), Waste Management Plans (WMP), Oil Spill Prevention and Response Plans, and related environmental procedures.
Familiarity with environmental impact assessment of process systems during drilling, construction, transportation, installation, commissioning, operation, and decommissioning.
Experience assessing environmental risks related to decommissioning, abandonment, and demolition of existing facilities.
Strong communication, presentation, and conflict management skills.
Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously while maintaining oversight of critical technical issues and risks.
Ability to identify technical issues and escalate them appropriately to project management.
Strong teamwork, collaboration, problem‑solving, and decision‑making capabilities.
Ability to identify engineering risks and develop appropriate mitigation plans to ensure project success.
B.Sc. in Environmental Engineering or Chemical Engineering from a recognized university.
Membership in a recognized professional engineering or HSE association/institution is preferred.
r: Responsible for environmental engineering and compliance activities associated with onshore greenfield and brownfield project scopes. Provides technical input across detailed engineering design, procurement, installation, construction, and commissioning of onshore facilities to ensure full adherence to applicable environmental standards and regulatory requirements, particularly for power generation & associated projects.
